Phase 6: Implicit Differentiation with ChainRules

Goal

Enable efficient reverse-mode AD for parameter gradients through implicit differentiation.

Mathematical Background

For a power flow solve: g(y, p) = 0 where y = solve(p)

To compute ∂loss/∂p when loss depends on y:

∂loss/∂p = ∂loss/∂y · dy/dp

By implicit function theorem:

g(y(p), p) = 0
dg = 0
(∂g/∂y)·dy + (∂g/∂p)·dp = 0
dy/dp = -(∂g/∂y)^-1 · (∂g/∂p)
     = -J^-1 · B

So:

∂loss/∂p = -∂loss/∂y · J^-1 · B
         = -λ^T · B

where λ = J^T \ (∂loss/∂y) (adjoint solve)

Computational cost: O(1) in number of parameters!

  • 1 adjoint solve: O(n) for sparse system
  • 1 matrix-vector product: O(nnz(B))

Implementation Tasks

Task 6.1: Define ChainRules rrule (~50 LOC)

File: src/powercore/parameter_chainrules.jl

using ChainRulesCore

"""
    power_flow_solve(psys::ParameterizedSystem, p::AbstractVector; kwargs...)

Solve power flow with given parameters.

Returns y such that g(y, p) = 0.

This function has an rrule for efficient reverse-mode AD.
"""
function power_flow_solve(psys::ParameterizedSystem, p::AbstractVector; kwargs...)
    # Scatter parameters to model fields
    scatter_parameters!(psys, p)

    # Solve power flow
    sys = psys.sys
    dae = DAE(Float64, sys)

    # Use NonlinearSolve or similar
    result = solve(NonlinearProblem(
        (g, y) -> begin
            copyto!(dae.y, y)
            ws = SystemResidualWorkspace(Float64, sys)
            evaluate_system_residuals!(ws, dae)
            copyto!(g, dae.g)
        end,
        dae.y;
        kwargs...
    )

    return result.zero
end

"""
    rrule for power_flow_solve

Implements implicit differentiation for reverse-mode AD.

# Algorithm
1. Forward pass: Solve g(y, p) = 0 for y
2. Reverse pass:
   - Given ȳ = ∂loss/∂y
   - Solve J^T λ = ȳ for λ (adjoint)
   - Compute p̄ = -λ^T · B where B = ∂g/∂p
"""
function ChainRulesCore.rrule(
    ::typeof(power_flow_solve),
    psys::ParameterizedSystem,
    p::AbstractVector;
    cache=nothing,
    kwargs...
)
    # Forward pass: solve for y
    y = power_flow_solve(psys, p; kwargs...)

    # Setup for reverse pass
    if isnothing(cache)
        # Create cache if not provided
        cache = CachedAutodiffWorkspace(psys.sys)
    end

    # Pullback function
    function power_flow_pullback(ȳ)
        # ȳ = ∂loss/∂y (upstream gradient)

        # Step 1: Compute Jacobian J = ∂g/∂y at solution
        sparsity_y = jacobian_sparsity_pattern(psys.sys)
        colors_y = matrix_colors(sparsity_y)
        J = Float64.(sparsity_y)

        # Use colored Jacobian
        forwarddiff_color_jacobian!(J, cache, y; colorvec=colors_y)

        # Step 2: Solve adjoint system J^T λ = ȳ
        λ = J' \ ȳ

        # Step 3: Compute parameter Jacobian B = ∂g/∂p
        if isnothing(psys.sparsity_dgdp)
            parameter_sparsity_pattern!(psys, cache)
        end
        B = Float64.(psys.sparsity_dgdp)
        compute_parameter_jacobian!(B, psys, cache, y, p)

        # Step 4: Chain rule: ∂loss/∂p = -λ^T · B
        p̄ = -B' * λ

        # Return gradients (NoTangent for function and psys)
        return (NoTangent(), NoTangent(), p̄)
    end

    return y, power_flow_pullback
end

Complexity:

  • Forward solve: O(n³) for dense or O(n) for sparse iterative
  • Adjoint solve: Same as forward
  • B computation: O(ncolors × evalcost), already cached
  • Matrix-vector: O(nnz(B))

Total: Dominated by solves, independent of number of parameters!

Task 6.2: Add Zygote/Enzyme compatibility (~20 LOC)

# Test with Zygote
using Zygote

function loss_function(p, psys)
    y = power_flow_solve(psys, p)

    # Extract bus voltages
    v = get_bus_voltages(psys.sys, y)

    # Loss: deviation from nominal voltage
    return sum((v .- 1.0).^2)
end

# Compute gradient via Zygote
grad = Zygote.gradient(p -> loss_function(p, psys), p0)

Task 6.3: Add @testitem for rrule verification (~80 LOC)

@testitem "ChainRules rrule" begin
    using Powerful
    using Powerful
    using ChainRulesCore
    using ChainRulesTestUtils

    # Load test case
    case = PowerFlowData.parse_network(joinpath(pkgdir(Powerful), "cases", "ieee14.raw"))
    bus = parse_model(Bus, case)
    pq = parse_model(PQ, case)
    pv = parse_model(PV, case)
    branch = parse_model(Branch, case)

    am = AddressManager()
    sys = SystemModel(am, (; Bus=bus, PQ=pq, PV=pv, Branch=branch))

    # Setup parameters
    psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
    add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :pg, [1, 3])
    finalize_parameters!(psys)

    p0 = gather_parameters(psys)

    # Test rrule
    test_rrule(power_flow_solve, psys, p0; rtol=1e-5)

    println("✓ ChainRules rrule verified")
end

Task 6.4: Benchmark vs forward-mode (~30 LOC)

Compare:

  • Forward-mode: ForwardDiff.gradient(f, p) → O(n_params) evaluations
  • Reverse-mode: Zygote.gradient(f, p) → O(1) evaluation

Expected speedup: ~100x for 100 parameters

Task 7.1: Droop Coefficient Tuning Example (~150 LOC)

File: examples/optimize_droop_coefficients.jl

"""
Tune PV generator droop coefficients to minimize voltage deviations.

Problem:
- Given: Power system with PV generators
- Optimize: Droop coefficients R for each generator
- Objective: Minimize voltage deviations from nominal (1.0 pu)
- Constraints: R ∈ [0.01, 0.10]

Uses implicit differentiation for efficient gradients.
"""

using Powerful, Optimization, OptimizationOptimJL

# Load system
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("ACTIVSg70k.raw", v=33)
sys = create_system(case)

# Setup parameters (droop coefficients)
psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
pv_indices = 1:100  # First 100 generators
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :droop_R, pv_indices)
finalize_parameters!(psys)

# Initial parameters
p0 = gather_parameters(psys)  # Current droop values

# Objective: minimize voltage deviations
function objective(p, psys)
    y = power_flow_solve(psys, p; ftol=1e-8)
    v = get_bus_voltages(psys.sys, y)
    return sum((v .- 1.0).^2)
end

# Optimize using Zygote for gradients
cache = CachedAutodiffWorkspace(psys.sys)
prob = OptimizationProblem(
    (p, _) -> objective(p, psys),
    p0;
    lb = fill(0.01, length(p0)),
    ub = fill(0.10, length(p0))
)

sol = solve(prob, BFGS(); maxiters=50)

println("Optimal droop coefficients: ", sol.u)
println("Final objective: ", sol.objective)

Task 7.2: Parameter Estimation from PMU Data (~200 LOC)

File: examples/parameter_estimation_pmu.jl

"""
Estimate transmission line parameters from PMU measurements.

Problem:
- Given: Voltage and current phasor measurements from PMUs
- Estimate: Line impedances (R, X) and shunt susceptances (B)
- Method: Nonlinear least squares

This example demonstrates:
- Parameter selection for network topology
- Using measurement data for calibration
- Handling real-world noise
"""

# Synthetic PMU data (in practice, load from CSV)
measurements = load_pmu_measurements("pmu_data.csv")

# Select parameters to estimate
psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
add_parameter!(psys, :Branch, :r, 1:50)  # Resistances
add_parameter!(psys, :Branch, :x, 1:50)  # Reactances
add_parameter!(psys, :Branch, :b, 1:50)  # Susceptances
finalize_parameters!(psys)

# Objective: fit to measurements
function measurement_error(p, psys, measurements)
    y = power_flow_solve(psys, p)

    # Extract voltages and currents
    v_calc = get_bus_voltages(psys.sys, y)
    i_calc = get_branch_currents(psys.sys, y)

    # Compare with measurements
    v_error = sum((v_calc .- measurements.v).^2)
    i_error = sum((i_calc .- measurements.i).^2)

    return v_error + i_error
end

# Solve
sol = optimize(p -> measurement_error(p, psys, measurements), p0, BFGS())

Risks & Mitigations

Risk 1: ChainRules compatibility issues

Mitigation: Start with simple rrule, test incrementally

Risk 2: Adjoint solve numerical stability

Mitigation: Use same solver settings as forward, add condition number checks

Risk 3: Example complexity vs clarity

Mitigation: Start simple, add complexity gradually, extensive comments

Risk 4: Documentation becomes stale

Mitigation: Use doctest, link examples to CI

Open Questions

  1. Should we support Enzyme.jl in addition to Zygote?

    • Pro: Better performance for some problems
    • Con: Additional complexity

  2. Should examples use real data or synthetic?

    • Leaning toward synthetic for reproducibility
    • Could add optional real-data examples

  3. GPU support for implicit differentiation?

    • Current focus: CPU
    • Future work: Extend to GPU
